title: (No AI) Google launches Gemini 4 Carbon with a ‘significant leap’ in cybersecurity
author: Emma Roth
content:
![An image showing the Gemini logo on a dark blue background](https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2025/03/STK255_Google_Gemini_A.jpg?quality=90&strip=all&crop=0,0,100,100)

Google has released its latest frontier model, Gemini 4 Carbon, offering "significant gains" in coding, agentic tasks, and cybersecurity. In [an announcement on Wednesday](https://blog.google/innovation-and-ai/models-and-research/gemini-models/introducing-gemini-4-carbon/), Google highlights Carbon's top spot on the [Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index (v5.0)](https://artificialanalysis.ai/evaluations/artificial-analysis-intelligence-index) benchmark, with Claude Opus 5.5 and GPT-6 Astra trailing behind.

The new Gemini 4 Carbon model offers improvements over Argon, which Google released earlier this month. It's currently only available to a select group of cybersecurity defense companies, but it will eventually expand to other partners [in its Fairwind Program](https://blog.google/innovation-and-ai/technology/safety-security/fairwind-program/).

![](https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/10/Artificial-Analysis-Intelligence-Index-Score-28-Oct-26.png?quality=90&strip=all&crop=0,0,100,100)

title: (No AI) Microsoft is ending Copilot support on smart TVs
author: Andrew Liszewski
content:
![Microsoft’s Copilot AI assistant shown running on a Samsung smart TV.](https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/10/copilot.jpg?quality=90&strip=all&crop=0,0,100,100)

Nearly two years after [LG and Samsung announced at CES 2025](https://www.theverge.com/2025/1/6/24337033/lg-samsung-microsoft-copilot-smart-tvs-ces-2025) that their latest smart TVs would include access to Microsoft's Copilot, the company is ending support for the AI assistant's functionality on all TVs this year, [according to a report by _Windows Central_](https://www.windowscentral.com/artificial-intelligence/microsoft-copilot/microsoft-is-killing-copilot-on-all-smart-tvs-after-backlash-and-strategy-shift-lg-confirms-support-will-end-before-2027).

The news comes not from an official announcement from LG, Samsung, or Microsoft, but from an on-screen notification that appeared on _Windows Central'_s Zac Bowden's webOS-powered LG TV earlier today. "Microsoft has recently decided to end support for Copilot functionality on all TVs, including the Copilot-enabled feature available on our LG TVs. As a result, the Copilot-enabled feat …
